# Map-Not-Encyclopedia Doctrine (gzkit)

> **Rule version:** `0.9.0` — dead-pointer sweep under GHI #533 (2026-09-01) — the § Budget destination no longer routes through a closed tracker. Prior 0.8.0 was the diet pass under GHI #921 (operator ruling 2026-08-29, *"we are compressing everything and anything that the agent can consume"*). Version history lifted to [Rule Version History](../../docs/governance/rule-version-history.md#agents-md-map-doctrinemd). Binding rules unchanged.

## Invariant

AGENTS.md MUST contain only (a) binding bullet rules (one bullet = one rule, ≤ 3 lines per bullet), (b) structured tables (Persona, Gate Covenant, OBPI kinds, canonical-invocations, defect-fix routing thresholds), and (c) canonical-link references to deeper documentation at stable URLs under `docs/governance/`. AGENTS.md MUST NOT contain (i) multi-paragraph rationale prose (paragraph > 5 lines without a binding-bullet anchor), (ii) worked examples or anti-pattern catalogs, (iii) "Why this is canon" / "Why X" coda blockquotes, (iv) narrative pedagogical sections, or (v) operative-claims expansions whose binding-bullet form already states the rule. CLAUDE.md inherits the same shape contract. `.claude/rules/*.md` files inherit the same shape with their existing 16k per-file budget.

## Five prohibited shapes

1. **Multi-paragraph rationale prose** — paragraph longer than 5 lines without a binding-bullet anchor. The rationale belongs in `docs/governance/`; the bullet states the rule.
2. **Worked examples or anti-pattern catalogs** — subsections titled "Worked example", "Anti-patterns", "Example", or equivalent. These belong in the canonical doctrine doc at a stable URL.
3. **"Why this is canon" / "Why X" coda blockquotes** — blockquote paragraphs that explain why a rule was chosen. These are encyclopedic; the bullet is the rule.
4. **Narrative pedagogical sections** — multi-paragraph explanations of how a rule works, its history, or its relationship to other rules. Route to `docs/governance/agent-contract-rationale.md`.
5. **Operative-claims expansions** — prose blocks restating operative claims whose binding-bullet form already states the rule fully. The binding bullet is sufficient; the expansion is accretion.

## Budget

The **live enforced budgets are the values in `data/instructions_files_budget.json`** — the single source of truth read by `gz validate --instructions-files-budget`. This doctrine never duplicates those numbers into prose: a duplicated number drifts from what is enforced (the exact drift ADR-0.0.54 closeout corrected). Read the JSON for the current enforced values.

The **destination** this doctrine sets for AGENTS.md is a tightened `15000`-char ceiling (the map, not the encyclopedia). That weight-halving is **not yet in force**: AGENTS.md currently sits above `15000` under a relaxed interim budget, and reaching the target is **deferred to `ADR-0.35.0-canon-entry-corpus-landing`** § Decision 3 — sections declare `corpus-owned` or `unowned`, the generator materializes owned sections from the corpus, and the unowned byte total is held in a **decrease-only ratchet**. The predecessor pointer to `ADR-0.0.37` is **retired**: that ADR is terminal (§ Terminal Disposition, 2026-07-18) and its registry-spine OBPIs were permanently withdrawn, so no weight-halving work can land under it. The intermediate hop through **GHI #533 is also retired**: that issue closed 2026-09-01 `superseded` into this ADR, having tracked a dependency (the registry-projection migration) that was itself withdrawn. Cite the ADR directly — a pointer through a closed tracker is the same dead-pointer shape this paragraph already records once.

The transitional window is **open but no longer slack**. The delivered-surface witness (GHI #712, `src/gzkit/governance/trust_audits/surface_delivery_witness.py`) is wired into the default `gz check` scope, and AGENTS.md sits **560 B** under the Codex `project_doc_max_bytes` default — growth past that boundary fails the default gate closed. Shape enforcement (`gz validate --agents-md-map-conformance`) ships and binds now; the weight target lands with the deferred work. (ADR-0.0.54 closed Completed-Partial on exactly this split.)

## Shape enforcement

`gz validate --agents-md-map-conformance` (OBPI-0.0.54-03, forthcoming) asserts:
- No paragraph in AGENTS.md is > 5 lines without a binding-bullet anchor
- No subsection title is in the prohibited set
- Every `See [text](path)` link resolves to an existing file
- File size is measured against the budget in `data/instructions_files_budget.json` and reported — **advisory, never blocking** (operator ruling 2026-08-17; the earlier "until 1.0" wording is retired, see the version note). The same posture binds `gz validate --instructions-files-budget`. The three criteria above stay fail-closed — the stay is scoped to budget limits, never to shape.
- Bringing an over-budget surface back into trim is the `instructions-files-diet` chore's job, on a cadence or on demand — **not** an ordinary session's. Ordinary sessions add to sources (`gz content remember`) and never resize a render surface.

Validator emits `RemediationPayload` with `recovery: /gz-context-diet` on any violation.

## Attestation granularity

Operator ruling 2026-08-17. **The discriminator is whether CANON changed — never whether a file was written.** A rendition is a Layer-3 derived view (`docs/governance/state-doctrine.md`; Architectural Boundary 6); the corpus is Layer-1. Attestation attaches to the canon change and to completed OBPI/ADR work, never to the projection.

| Act | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Re-render of **unchanged** canon | **No attestation.** Corpus fingerprint unmoved; `--rendition-floor-coherence` already proves every `tier: invariant` entry survived verbatim. The chore completes it. |
| **Adding** a corpus entry (`gz content remember`) | **Attested** — recorded provenance |
| **Removing** an entry (`gz content retire`) | **Attested** — recorded provenance |
| **Trim / compression** to fit a delivery cap | **Invites operator review.** It changes what canon *looks like* without changing what canon *is*. |

- **A GHI needs no attestation.** Operator verbatim: *"I only attest to completed obpi/adr work."* The GHI is the work order and the receipt (AGENTS.md § Operator Doctrine).
- **Do not call a build step "Gate 5." The content surface's attestation is named CORPUS ATTESTATION.** Gate 5 is OBPI/ADR completion attestation (ADR-0.0.36) and nothing else; a second subject wearing one name is the collision the transit/exchange/handoff fence forbids. `gz content commit --help` claimed the name until 2026-08-18 and no longer does (GHI #822). The replacement noun is `corpus`, not `rendition`, because this same ruling puts the attestable subject on the corpus — the table above attests adding and removing entries and exempts a re-render — and holds a rendition to be a Layer-3 derived view, never the thing attested. Naming a rendition promotion after the artifact it writes would re-assert the very inversion this section records.
- **Attestation on add/remove is recorded provenance, never a blocking gate.** `ADR-0.35.0` § Decision 7 stands unchanged: *"Capture must never be blocked: losing the operator's words is strictly worse than a red tree."* The ledger records whose canon it is; the capture still always succeeds.
- **The transport never gates the attestation.** An operator ruling given in session and relayed verbatim via `--attestation-text` IS the attestation (AGENTS.md § Operator Doctrine, the TTY/PTY prohibition). "The operator is not at a terminal" is never a reason a chore cannot complete.

**(Advisory — the implementation is inverted and no witness holds it.)** Measured 2026-08-17: `gz content remember` and `gz content retire` accept no `--attestor`; `gz content commit` requires one and fail-closes on empty. So the two acts this rule makes attested are ungated, and the one it exempts is gated. Reclassify when the verbs carry the granularity.
